why: Running the same three lines again shifts the array right a second time, so it does not undo the shift. For example, [1,2,3] becomes [3,1,2] and then [2,3,1], not [1,2,3]. The answer treats the shift as its own inverse, which is a wrong rule. Undoing it needs a left rotation: save x[0], copy x[i] = x[i+1] for i from 0 to length-2, then set x[length-1] to the saved value.
